content:
Nick (AM): Hey team — FinEdge POC kickoff today. They want Private deployment (VPCs in their account) and are weighing simple VPC peering vs PrivateLink interface endpoints vs Transit Gateway. Key asks: preserve fast TLS passthrough for client connections, split-horizon DNS for internal hostnames, MTU issues across on-prem VPN, and rough egress cost expectations for sizing the POC. Also got a 30-question security questionnaire (KMS/HSM, audit logs, network segmentation). Any quick guidance we can hand to their network ops so they can unblock the PoC?

Alex D.: For a small number of VPCs (1-2) and simple ingress from their apps, PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is lowest friction — no routable peering, per-AZ ENIs, easier to lock down with SGs. If they have >5 VPCs or multiple accounts, TGW gives simpler central routing and better throughput. Peering is fine but gets messy at scale.

Alex D.: On TLS passthrough — we can support SNI passthrough to customer backends if they terminate TLS; if Redwood terminates TLS (for hosted mode) you'll need NLB with TCP passthrough or TLS termination at ALB. For Private deployment we usually let the customer terminate TLS inside their VPC.

Sanjay R.: MTU — common gotcha over IPsec/SD-WAN tunnels. Recommend testing with 1400B first. If they see fragmentation, drop to 1380 on tunnel or enable TCP MSS clamping on their firewall. Quick test command they can run from a bastion: `ping -M do -s 1400 <peer-ip>`

Alex D.: DNS: split-horizon is the usual pattern — private Route53 (or their internal resolver) returning internal hostnames for the interface endpoint FQDNs. Don’t use public DNS for private endpoints. TTLs should be low (30s-60s) during POC because we sometimes rotate endpoints during canary.

Alex D.: Example minimal firewall allowlist we give to customers (they asked for a template):

```
# Allow outbound to Redwood Private endpoints (example)
#  - HTTPS for API traffic
#  - NTP for time sync (if required)
#  - DNS to resolver IPs

ALLOW TCP 443 to *.redwood-inference-private.redwoodapi.net
ALLOW TCP 443 to 198.51.100.0/24  # example endpoint ENI range (replace with actual)
ALLOW UDP 123 to 203.0.113.12      # ntp.example (optional)
ALLOW UDP 53 to 10.0.0.2,10.0.0.3  # internal resolvers
```

Maria P.: Pricing: for Private deployments you get a baseline platform fee + egress. For AWS-like clouds expect egress band to dominate at scale — rough ballpark for sizing the POC: 100-500 GB/month is trivial, 1-5 TB/month starts to show line-item costs. I can pull a tailored estimate if you share expected token/GB throughput. Also call out dedicated connector (per-hour) vs shared connector pricing — that affects hourly commitment during the POC.

Nick (AM): Good. Can you prepare a 1-page network ops checklist I can send to their infra team? They want a checklist before the security questionnaire answers.

Sanjay R.: I’ll draft checklist: items = collector of their network contact, desired topology (peering/privatelink/tgw), MTU test, DNS delegation plan, allowlist + example SG rules, bastion for connectivity tests, scheduled 1-hour maintenance window for canary.

security-bot: Security quick notes — we support customer-managed KMS keys (bring-your-own) and HSM integrations for Private deployments. Audit logs are shipped to customer S3/CloudStorage and can be integrated with their SIEM. Share the exact questionnaire and I’ll pre-fill standard answers.

infra-bot: FYI — when using interface endpoints we allocate ENIs in each AZ. If they have strict IP allowlists, we need their ASN/ENI IP ranges; otherwise provide domain-based allowlist.

Maria P.: I’ve got a rough POC cost sheet ready. Nick, can you DM the estimated throughput (tokens/min or GB/day)? I’ll convert to an expected monthly cost and note where dedicated connector commits change the math.

Nick (AM): Will do — looping in FinEdge network lead (cc @FinEdge-Net) in DM for the IPs and expected throughput. Aim to send checklist + security draft by EOD. :thumbsup:

Alex D.: One more: if they plan heavy egress to other cloud regions, prefer TGW or direct connect equivalents to avoid cross-account ENI egress charge surprises.

Nick (AM): Perfect. Thanks team — pushing checklist now and will follow up with the questionnaire file.
